items.followUp: Define molecular formula and give an example.

rubric.why: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as showing the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it gives the simplest ratio or proportion of atoms.

rubric.why: CH₂O is the empirical formula of glucose.
rubric.description: Gives a valid empirical formula example, such as CH₂O for glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
For example, the empirical formula of glucose (C6H12O6) is CH2O.

items.followUp: Why are noble gases generally chemically stable?

rubric.why: A complete outer electron shell is the key electronic feature of noble gases.
rubric.description: States that noble gases have completely filled outermost (valence) electron shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the filled outer shell.

rubric.why: The filled shell makes noble gases stable and gives them little tendency to react.
rubric.description: Links the filled outer shell to stability or to a low tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining why they are generally unreactive.

modelAnswer: Noble gases have completely filled outermost electron shells.
Therefore, they have little tendency to gain, lose or share electrons and are generally unreactive.
